area.scope.heading: The same repair costs differently in a greystone, a cottage and a new build
area.scope.1.why: Greystones facing the park often still heat with a boiler and radiators; many rehabbed two-flats and cottages run furnaces.
area.scope.2.why: Newer Humboldt Park condos often run heat pumps, which heat and cool. The repair depends on which half has failed.
area.scope.3.why: In a greystone split into condos, one boiler can serve every unit, so the owners decide on repairs together.
area.scope.4.why: Furnaces sit in low basements west of the park; condensers go in gangways or on garage roofs off the alley.
area.scope.5.why: Shops and restaurants on the Paseo run rooftop units and kitchen exhaust, so roof access and opening hours set the work.
area.scope.6.why: The biggest swing of all. Where the unit has years left, we say so.

area.buildings.heading: What heats and cools your Humboldt Park building
area.buildings.1.title: Greystone two-flat
area.buildings.1.body: A boiler and radiators, or a furnace per unit after conversion. Condensers off the alley.
area.buildings.2.title: Frame cottage
area.buildings.2.body: Usually a basement furnace with central air, sometimes a boiler. Low basements and short duct runs.
area.buildings.3.title: New-build condo
area.buildings.3.body: A furnace or heat pump per unit, with central air. Condensers on the roof or a rear deck.
area.buildings.4.title: Storefront with flats
area.buildings.4.body: Rooftop units for the shop on Division or North Ave, a furnace or boiler for the flats above.

area.faq.heading: Humboldt Park HVAC, answered
area.faq.1.q: Is the boiler in my greystone worth repairing, or does it need replacing?
area.faq.1.a: Often it's worth repairing. We diagnose first, and where the boiler has years left, we say so. Replacement is quoted only when the repair stops making sense.
area.faq.2.q: How far is your shop from Humboldt Park?
area.faq.3.q: Do you work on heat pumps in newer Humboldt Park condos?
area.faq.4.q: Does HVAC repair in Chicago need a permit?
area.cta.body: Have the make of your boiler, furnace or heat pump to hand, and tell us what it's doing. For a storefront on Division, mention how we get onto the roof.

extras.faq.2.a: About 1.5 miles. The shop is at 1225 N Cleaver St, east of the corner at Division and Rockwell, and Rob runs the calls from there.
extras.faq.3.a: Yes. Heat pumps are on our service list for both heating and cooling. Have the make and model to hand when you call, and tell us where the outdoor unit sits.
extras.faq.4.a: No. Chicago doesn't require a permit to repair, diagnose or maintain heating and cooling. Permits cover installs and construction, so a company's permit count says little about its repair work.

_sources.boundaries: City of Chicago neighborhood polygon 'Humboldt Park' (y6yq-dbs2): Bloomingdale / The 606 (north), the Union Pacific tracks along Kinzie (south), the rail line between Kostner and Cicero, at Kenton (west), Rockwell (east). 81% is community area 23, 19% West Town (24). Wikipedia (Humboldt Park, Chicago): community area 23 runs from Bloomingdale to the UP tracks and from the tracks between Kostner and Cicero to California; East Humboldt Park (Sacramento to Western) is officially in West Town.
_sources.districts: Wikipedia (Humboldt Park, Chicago): Paseo Boricua on Division, East and West Humboldt Park split at Sacramento, the 207-acre park. Block Club Chicago (2022) and Chicago Landmarks (Paseo Boricua Gateway Flags report): the flags bookend Division between Western and California. K streets: Wikipedia (K-Town).
_sources.buildings: Wikipedia: the park is lined with greystones; Chicago magazine: greystones along the boulevard system, e.g. 2845 W Division; 1127 N Sacramento on the boulevard facing the park. Chicago YIMBY: 2709 W Division, apartments over retail on the Paseo. Area permit mix (furnace 12, heat pump 9, ductwork 8) for the furnace and heat-pump new builds.
